sanskrit: yeṣāṃ nāgrabhujo viprā devatātithibālakāḥ rākṣasān eva tān viddhi nirvaṣaṭkāramaṅgalān
english: Those whose Brāhmaṇas, gods, guests, and children eat no portion offered first—know them to be very rākṣasas, devoid of the auspicious vaṣaṭ-call.

sanskrit: tasmād agraṃ prayaccheta devebhyaḥ pratipūjitam śirasā praṇataś cāpi hared balim atandritaḥ
english: Therefore one should offer the first portion, duly honored, to the gods, and bowing his head should present the oblation untiringly.

sanskrit: gṛhyā hi devatā nityam āśaṃsanti gṛhāt sadā bāhyāś cāgantavo ye 'nye yakṣarākṣasapannagāḥ
english: For the household deities ever look in hope toward the home, and so too the outer comers, the other beings—Yakṣas, Rākṣasas, and serpents.

sanskrit: ito dattena jīvanti devatāḥ pitaras tathā te prītāḥ prīṇayanty etān āyuṣā yaśasā dhanaiḥ
english: By what is given from here the gods and the ancestors live, and being pleased they gratify these givers with long life, with fame, and with wealth.

sanskrit: balayaḥ saha puṣpais tu devānām upahārayet dadhidrapsayutāḥ puṇyāḥ sugandhāḥ priyadarśanāḥ
english: To the gods one should present oblations together with flowers—holy ones graced with drops of curds, sweet-scented and fair to behold.

sanskrit: kāryā rudhiramāṃsāḍhyā balayo yakṣarakṣasām surāsavapuraskārā lājollepanabhūṣitāḥ
english: For the Yakṣas and Rākṣasas the oblations should be rich in blood and flesh, set forth with wine and liquor and adorned with parched grain and unguents.

sanskrit: nāgānāṃ dayitā nityaṃ padmotpalavimiśritāḥ tilān guḍasusaṃpannān bhūtānām upahārayet
english: For the serpents, ever dear to them, oblations mingled with lotuses and water-lilies; and to the spirits one should present sesame well supplied with molasses.

sanskrit: agradātāgrabhogī syād balavarṇasamanvitaḥ tasmād agraṃ prayaccheta devebhyaḥ pratipūjitam
english: He who gives the first portion shall himself enjoy the first portion, endowed with strength and beauty; therefore let him offer the first portion, duly honored, to the gods.

sanskrit: jvalaty aharaho veśma yāś cāsya gṛhadevatāḥ tāḥ pūjyā bhūtikāmena prasṛtāgrapradāyinā
english: Day after day his dwelling blazes with light; and those household deities of his are to be worshipped by one who desires welfare, by him who offers the foremost portion outstretched.

sanskrit: ity etad asurendrāya kāvyaḥ provāca bhārgavaḥ suvarṇāya manuḥ prāha suvarṇo nāradāya ca
english: Thus did the descendant of Bhṛgu, Kāvya, declare this to the lord of the Asuras; Manu told it to Suvarṇa, and Suvarṇa to Nārada.

sanskrit: nārado 'pi mayi prāha guṇān etān mahādyute tvam apy etad viditveha sarvam ācara putraka
english: And Nārada too told these virtues to me, O greatly resplendent one; do you also, having understood all this here, act upon it, my son.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca śrutaṃ me bharataśreṣṭha puṣpadhūpapradāyinām phalaṃ balividhāne ca tad bhūyo vaktum arhasi
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: I have heard, O best of the Bhāratas, the fruit of those who offer flowers and incense, and the rule of oblation; you should tell me more of it.

sanskrit: dhūpapradānasya phalaṃ pradīpasya tathaiva ca balayaś ca kimarthaṃ vai kṣipyante gṛhamedhibhiḥ
english: What is the fruit of giving incense, and likewise of the lamp, and for what purpose are oblations cast forth by householders?

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca atrāpy udāharantīmam itihāsaṃ purātanam nahuṣaṃ prati saṃvādam agastyasya bhṛgos tathā
english: Bhīṣma said: On this too they recount an ancient tale—the colloquy of Agastya and of Bhṛgu concerning Nahuṣa.

sanskrit: nahuṣo hi mahārāja rājarṣiḥ sumahātapāḥ devarājyam anuprāptaḥ sukṛteneha karmaṇā
english: For Nahuṣa, O great king, a royal sage of mighty austerity, had attained the sovereignty of the gods by his good deeds here.

sanskrit: tatrāpi prayato rājan nahuṣas tridive vasan mānuṣīś caiva divyāś ca kurvāṇo vividhāḥ kriyāḥ
english: There too, O king, Nahuṣa, dwelling in the third heaven, remained devout, performing manifold rites both human and divine.

sanskrit: mānuṣyas tatra sarvāḥ sma kriyās tasya mahātmanaḥ pravṛttās tridive rājan divyāś caiva sanātanāḥ
english: All those human rites of that great-souled one continued in the third heaven, O king, as did the eternal divine ones.

sanskrit: agnikāryāṇi samidhaḥ kuśāḥ sumanasas tathā balayaś cānnalājābhir dhūpanaṃ dīpakarma ca
english: Fire-rites, kindling-sticks, kuśa grass and flowers, oblations with food and parched grain, the burning of incense and the offering of lamps—

sanskrit: sarvaṃ tasya gṛhe rājñaḥ prāvartata mahātmanaḥ japayajñān manoyajñāṃs tridive 'pi cakāra saḥ
english: all this went on in the house of that great-souled king; and even in the third heaven he performed sacrifices of muttered prayer and sacrifices of the mind.

sanskrit: daivatāny arcayaṃś cāpi vidhivat sa sureśvaraḥ sarvāṇy eva yathānyāyaṃ yathāpūrvam ariṃdama
english: And that lord of the gods worshipped all the deities according to rule, each in its proper manner as of old, O subduer of foes.

sanskrit: athendrasya bhaviṣyatvād ahaṃkāras tam āviśat sarvāś caiva kriyās tasya paryahīyanta bhūpate
english: Then, through his having become Indra, pride entered into him, and all his rites began to fall away, O ruler of the earth.

sanskrit: sa ṛṣīn vāhayām āsa varadānamadānvitaḥ parihīnakriyaś cāpi durbalatvam upeyivān
english: Drunk with the boon that had been granted him, he made the sages bear him as draught-animals; and lapsing from his rites, he came into weakness.

sanskrit: tasya vāhayataḥ kālo munimukhyāṃs tapodhanān ahaṃkārābhibhūtasya sumahān atyavartata
english: As he, overcome by pride, made the foremost sages rich in austerity bear him, a very long time passed by.

sanskrit: atha paryāyaśa ṛṣīn vāhanāyopacakrame paryāyaś cāpy agastyasya samapadyata bhārata
english: Then he began to yoke the sages by turns to draw him, and the turn of Agastya too came round, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: athāgamya mahātejā bhṛgur brahmavidāṃ varaḥ agastyam āśramasthaṃ vai samupetyedam abravīt
english: Then Bhṛgu of great splendor, best of the knowers of Brahman, came and, approaching Agastya who was in his hermitage, spoke thus.

sanskrit: evaṃ vayam asatkāraṃ devendrasyāsya durmateḥ nahuṣasya kimarthaṃ vai marṣayāma mahāmune
english: Why, O great sage, should we endure this insolence of Nahuṣa, this evil-minded lord of the gods?

sanskrit: agastya uvāca katham eṣa mayā śakyaḥ śaptuṃ yasya mahāmune varadena varo datto bhavato viditaś ca saḥ
english: Agastya said: How can this one be cursed by me, O great sage, to whom a boon was granted by the boon-giver—a boon known to you?

sanskrit: yo me dṛṣṭipathaṃ gacchet sa me vaśyo bhaved iti ity anena varo devād yācito gacchatā divam
english: "Whoever shall come within the path of my gaze, let him fall under my power"—such was the boon this one begged of the god as he went up to heaven.

sanskrit: evaṃ na dagdhaḥ sa mayā bhavatā ca na saṃśayaḥ anyenāpy ṛṣimukhyena na śapto na ca pātitaḥ
english: So he has not been burned by me, nor, beyond doubt, by you; nor has he been cursed or cast down by any other foremost sage.

sanskrit: amṛtaṃ caiva pānāya dattam asmai purā vibho mahātmane tadarthaṃ ca nāsmābhir vinipātyate
english: And of old the nectar was given him to drink, O mighty one; for that reason this great-souled one is not cast down by us.

sanskrit: prāyacchata varaṃ devaḥ prajānāṃ duḥkhakārakam dvijeṣv adharmayuktāni sa karoti narādhamaḥ
english: The god granted a boon that brings sorrow to creatures; that basest of men commits deeds of unrighteousness against the twice-born.

sanskrit: atra yat prāptakālaṃ nas tad brūhi vadatāṃ vara bhavāṃś cāpi yathā brūyāt kurvīmahi tathā vayam
english: Tell us what is fitting for the occasion in this matter, O best of speakers; and as you may direct, so shall we act.

sanskrit: bhṛgur uvāca pitāmahaniyogena bhavantam aham āgataḥ pratikartuṃ balavati nahuṣe darpam āsthite
english: Bhṛgu said: By the command of the Grandsire I have come to you, that we may retaliate now that mighty Nahuṣa is set upon his arrogance.

sanskrit: adya hi tvā sudurbuddhī rathe yokṣyati devarāṭ adyainam aham udvṛttaṃ kariṣye 'nindram ojasā
english: This very day that most evil-minded king of the gods will yoke you to his chariot; this very day, by my power, I shall make the upstart no longer Indra.

sanskrit: adyendraṃ sthāpayiṣyāmi paśyatas te śatakratum saṃcālya pāpakarmāṇam indrasthānāt sudurmatim
english: This day, before your eyes, I shall set Indra of the hundred sacrifices in his place, dislodging the evil-doing, most wicked-minded one from the station of Indra.

sanskrit: adya cāsau kudevendras tvāṃ padā dharṣayiṣyati daivopahatacittatvād ātmanāśāya mandadhīḥ
english: And this day that false lord of the gods will strike you with his foot—dull-witted, his mind smitten by fate, working his own ruin.

sanskrit: vyutkrāntadharmaṃ tam ahaṃ dharṣaṇāmarṣito bhṛśam ahir bhavasveti ruṣā śapsye pāpaṃ dvijadruham
english: Him who has transgressed dharma, that sinner and enemy of the twice-born, I—made wrathful past bearing by his outrage—shall curse in fury, saying, "Become a serpent!"

sanskrit: tata enaṃ sudurbuddhiṃ dhikśabdābhihatatviṣam dharaṇyāṃ pātayiṣyāmi prekṣatas te mahāmune
english: Then that most evil-minded one, his radiance struck down by the word of shame, I shall hurl to the earth before your eyes, O great sage—

sanskrit: nahuṣaṃ pāpakarmāṇam aiśvaryabalamohitam yathā ca rocate tubhyaṃ tathā kartāsmy ahaṃ mune
english: Nahuṣa, the evil-doer, deluded by lordship and might; and as it pleases you, so shall I do it, O sage.

sanskrit: evam uktas tu bhṛguṇā maitrāvaruṇir avyayaḥ agastyaḥ paramaprīto babhūva vigatajvaraḥ
english: Thus addressed by Bhṛgu, the imperishable son of Mitra and Varuṇa, Agastya, became greatly pleased and freed of his distress.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca kathaṃ sa vai vipannaś ca kathaṃ vai pātito bhuvi kathaṃ cānindratāṃ prāptas tad bhavān vaktum arhati
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: How was he undone, and how was he cast down upon the earth, and how did he come to lose his Indra-hood? This you should tell me.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca evaṃ tayoḥ saṃvadatoḥ kriyās tasya mahātmanaḥ sarvā evābhyavartanta yā divyā yāś ca mānuṣāḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: While the two were thus conversing, all the rites of that great-souled one were going forward—those that were divine and those that were human.

sanskrit: tathaiva dīpadānāni sarvopakaraṇāni ca balikarma ca yac cānyad utsekāś ca pṛthagvidhāḥ sarvās tasya samutpannā devarājño mahātmanaḥ
english: Likewise the gifts of lamps and all the appurtenances, the rite of oblation and whatever else, and libations of various kinds—all these arose for that great-souled king of the gods.

sanskrit: devaloke nṛloke ca sadācārā budhaiḥ smṛtāḥ te ced bhavanti rājendra ṛdhyante gṛhamedhinaḥ dhūpapradānair dīpaiś ca namaskārais tathaiva ca
english: In the world of the gods and the world of men, good observances are taught by the wise; if these are kept, O king of kings, householders prosper—through gifts of incense and of lamps, and likewise through acts of homage.

sanskrit: yathā siddhasya cānnasya dvijāyāgraṃ pradīyate balayaś ca gṛhoddeśe ataḥ prīyanti devatāḥ
english: As the first portion of cooked food is given to a Brāhmaṇa, and as oblations are set within the precincts of the house—by this the deities are pleased.

sanskrit: yathā ca gṛhiṇas toṣo bhaved vai balikarmaṇā tathā śataguṇā prītir devatānāṃ sma jāyate
english: And as great as is the householder's own satisfaction in the rite of oblation, a delight a hundredfold greater arises among the deities.

sanskrit: evaṃ dhūpapradānaṃ ca dīpadānaṃ ca sādhavaḥ praśaṃsanti namaskārair yuktam ātmaguṇāvaham
english: Thus the good praise the giving of incense and the giving of lamps, joined with acts of homage, as bringing virtue to the self.

sanskrit: snānenādbhiś ca yat karma kriyate vai vipaścitā namaskāraprayuktena tena prīyanti devatāḥ gṛhyāś ca devatāḥ sarvāḥ prīyante vidhinārcitāḥ
english: By the rite that the wise man performs with bathing and with water, joined with acts of homage, the deities are pleased; and all the household deities, worshipped according to rule, are gratified.

sanskrit: ity etāṃ buddhim āsthāya nahuṣaḥ sa nareśvaraḥ surendratvaṃ mahat prāpya kṛtavān etad adbhutam
english: Holding to this understanding, that lord of men, Nahuṣa, having attained the great lordship of the gods, accomplished this marvel.

sanskrit: kasya cit tv atha kālasya bhāgyakṣaya upasthite sarvam etad avajñāya na cakāraitad īdṛśam
english: But after some while, when the wasting of his fortune drew near, he scorned all this and no longer did such as this.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa parihīṇo 'bhūt surendro balikarmataḥ dhūpadīpodakavidhiṃ na yathāvac cakāra ha tato 'sya yajñaviṣayo rakṣobhiḥ paryabādhyata
english: Then that lord of the gods fell away from the rite of oblation; he no longer performed the observance of incense, lamp, and water as was fitting; and thereupon the sphere of his sacrifice was beset by Rākṣasas.

sanskrit: athāgastyam ṛṣiśreṣṭhaṃ vāhanāyājuhāva ha drutaṃ sarasvatīkūlāt smayann iva mahābalaḥ
english: Then that mighty one, as if smiling, summoned in haste Agastya, the best of sages, from the bank of the Sarasvatī, to draw his vehicle.

sanskrit: tato bhṛgur mahātejā maitrāvaruṇim abravīt nimīlayasva nayane jaṭā yāvad viśāmi te
english: Then Bhṛgu of great splendor said to the son of Mitra and Varuṇa: "Close your eyes, while I enter into your matted locks."

sanskrit: sthāṇubhūtasya tasyātha jaṭāḥ prāviśad acyutaḥ bhṛguḥ sa sumahātejāḥ pātanāya nṛpasya ha
english: Then, while Agastya stood motionless as a post, the unfailing Bhṛgu of mighty splendor entered into his matted locks, to bring about the king's downfall.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa devarāṭ prāptas tam ṛṣiṃ vāhanāya vai tato 'gastyaḥ surapatiṃ vākyam āha viśāṃ pate
english: Then that king of the gods came up to the sage to make him draw his car; and thereupon Agastya spoke this word to the lord of the gods, O lord of peoples.

sanskrit: yojayasvendra māṃ kṣipraṃ kaṃ ca deśaṃ vahāmi te yatra vakṣyasi tatra tvāṃ nayiṣyāmi surādhipa
english: "Yoke me quickly, O Indra; and to what region shall I bear you? Wherever you shall bid, there will I carry you, O lord of the gods."

sanskrit: ity ukto nahuṣas tena yojayām āsa taṃ munim bhṛgus tasya jaṭāsaṃstho babhūva hṛṣito bhṛśam
english: Thus addressed by him, Nahuṣa yoked that sage; and Bhṛgu, lodged within his matted locks, was exceedingly glad.

sanskrit: na cāpi darśanaṃ tasya cakāra sa bhṛgus tadā varadānaprabhāvajño nahuṣasya mahātmanaḥ
english: Nor then did Bhṛgu let himself be seen, knowing the power of the boon granted to the great-souled Nahuṣa.

sanskrit: na cukopa sa cāgastyo yukto 'pi nahuṣeṇa vai taṃ tu rājā pratodena codayām āsa bhārata
english: And Agastya, though yoked by Nahuṣa, did not grow angry; yet the king goaded him with the whip, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: na cukopa sa dharmātmā tataḥ pādena devarāṭ agastyasya tadā kruddho vāmenābhyahanac chiraḥ
english: That righteous one did not grow angry; then the king of the gods, in wrath, struck Agastya's head with his left foot.

sanskrit: tasmiñ śirasy abhihate sa jaṭāntargato bhṛguḥ śaśāpa balavat kruddho nahuṣaṃ pāpacetasam
english: When that head was struck, Bhṛgu, hidden within the matted locks, sorely enraged, cursed the evil-hearted Nahuṣa.

sanskrit: bhṛgur uvāca yasmāt padāhanaḥ krodhāc chirasīmaṃ mahāmunim tasmād āśu mahīṃ gaccha sarpo bhūtvā sudurmate
english: Bhṛgu said: Since in wrath you struck this great sage upon the head with your foot, therefore become a serpent and go swiftly to the earth, O most wicked-minded one!

sanskrit: ity uktaḥ sa tadā tena sarpo bhūtvā papāta ha adṛṣṭenātha bhṛguṇā bhūtale bharatarṣabha
english: Thus addressed by him, by Bhṛgu unseen, he then became a serpent and fell to the surface of the earth, O bull of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: bhṛguṃ hi yadi so 'drākṣīn nahuṣaḥ pṛthivīpate na sa śakto 'bhaviṣyad vai pātane tasya tejasā
english: For had Nahuṣa beheld Bhṛgu, O lord of the earth, he would not have had the power to cast him down by his splendor.

sanskrit: sa tu tais taiḥ pradānaiś ca tapobhir niyamais tathā patito 'pi mahārāja bhūtale smṛtimān abhūt prasādayām āsa bhṛguṃ śāpānto me bhaved iti
english: But by those various gifts and austerities and observances, though fallen to the earth, O great king, he remained possessed of his memory and besought Bhṛgu's grace, saying, "Let there be an end to my curse."

sanskrit: tato 'gastyaḥ kṛpāviṣṭaḥ prāsādayata taṃ bhṛgum śāpāntārthaṃ mahārāja sa ca prādāt kṛpānvitaḥ
english: Then Agastya, moved by compassion, entreated Bhṛgu for the ending of the curse, O great king; and he, filled with pity, granted it.

sanskrit: bhṛgur uvāca rājā yudhiṣṭhiro nāma bhaviṣyati kurūdvahaḥ sa tvāṃ mokṣayitā śāpād ity uktvāntaradhīyata
english: Bhṛgu said: A king named Yudhiṣṭhira, upholder of the Kurus, shall arise; he will release you from the curse. So saying, he vanished.

sanskrit: agastyo 'pi mahātejāḥ kṛtvā kāryaṃ śatakratoḥ svam āśramapadaṃ prāyāt pūjyamāno dvijātibhiḥ
english: And Agastya of great splendor, having accomplished the purpose of Indra of the hundred sacrifices, went to his own hermitage, honored by the twice-born.

sanskrit: nahuṣo 'pi tvayā rājaṃs tasmāc chāpāt samuddhṛtaḥ jagāma brahmasadanaṃ paśyatas te janādhipa
english: And Nahuṣa too, O king, delivered by you from that curse, went to the abode of Brahmā before your very eyes, O ruler of men.

sanskrit: tadā tu pātayitvā taṃ nahuṣaṃ bhūtale bhṛguḥ jagāma brahmasadanaṃ brahmaṇe ca nyavedayat
english: But then, having cast Nahuṣa down to the earth, Bhṛgu went to the abode of Brahmā and reported the matter to Brahmā.

sanskrit: tataḥ śakraṃ samānāyya devān āha pitāmahaḥ varadānān mama surā nahuṣo rājyam āptavān sa cāgastyena kruddhena bhraṃśito bhūtalaṃ gataḥ
english: Then the Grandsire, having brought Śakra back, said to the gods: "O gods, through a boon of mine Nahuṣa won the kingship, and he, cast down by the wrathful Agastya, has gone to the surface of the earth."

sanskrit: na ca śakyaṃ vinā rājñā surā vartayituṃ kva cit tasmād ayaṃ punaḥ śakro devarājye 'bhiṣicyatām
english: "And the gods can in no wise abide without a king; therefore let this Śakra again be consecrated to the sovereignty of the gods."

sanskrit: evaṃ saṃbhāṣamāṇaṃ tu devāḥ pārtha pitāmaham evam astv iti saṃhṛṣṭāḥ pratyūcus te pitāmaham
english: As the Grandsire spoke thus, O Pārtha, the gods, rejoicing, answered the Grandsire, "So be it."

sanskrit: so 'bhiṣikto bhagavatā devarājyena vāsavaḥ brahmaṇā rājaśārdūla yathāpūrvaṃ vyarocata
english: Consecrated to the sovereignty of the gods by the blessed Brahmā, Vāsava, O tiger among kings, shone forth as before.

sanskrit: evam etat purāvṛttaṃ nahuṣasya vyatikramāt sa ca tair eva saṃsiddho nahuṣaḥ karmabhiḥ punaḥ
english: Thus did this come to pass of old, through Nahuṣa's transgression; and by those very deeds was Nahuṣa once more made perfect.

sanskrit: tasmād dīpāḥ pradātavyāḥ sāyaṃ vai gṛhamedhibhiḥ divyaṃ cakṣur avāpnoti pretya dīpapradāyakaḥ pūrṇacandrapratīkāśā dīpadāś ca bhavanty uta
english: Therefore lamps should be offered at evening by householders; the giver of lamps obtains the divine eye after death, and those who give lamps come to be radiant as the full moon.

sanskrit: yāvad akṣinimeṣāṇi jvalate tāvatīḥ samāḥ rūpavān dhanavāṃś cāpi naro bhavati dīpadaḥ
english: For as many twinklings of the eye as the lamp burns, for so many years does the giver of the lamp become a man of beauty and of wealth.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca brāhmaṇasvāni ye mandā haranti bharatarṣabha nṛśaṃsakāriṇo mūḍhāḥ kva te gacchanti mānavāḥ
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: Those dull men who steal the property of Brāhmaṇas, O bull of the Bhāratas—the cruel-doing, deluded—whither do such men go?

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca atrāpy udāharantīmam itihāsaṃ purātanam caṇḍālasya ca saṃvādaṃ kṣatrabandhoś ca bhārata
english: Bhīṣma said: On this too they recount an ancient tale—the colloquy of a Caṇḍāla and a base-born Kṣatriya, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: rājanya uvāca vṛddharūpo 'si caṇḍāla bālavac ca viceṣṭase śvakharāṇāṃ rajaḥsevī kasmād udvijase gavām
english: The man of royal birth said: You are of aged aspect, O Caṇḍāla, yet you behave like a child; you who haunt the dust of dogs and donkeys—why do you shrink from cattle?
